tools.name: get_progression
tools.description: Read milestone/XP progress, unspent Development Points, purchased node names, and the current Development Tree frontier. The default shows the frontier; pass service to inspect one service tree in full. Use this after a milestone or when an advanced service is locked.

service.description: Optional service name or unambiguous substring, such as Electricity or Water & Sewage, to inspect that service's full development tree

tools.name: purchase_development_node
tools.description: Purchase one eligible Development Tree node by name from get_progression, spending legitimately earned points to unlock it. Eligibility needs points, service availability and prerequisites.

name.description: Development node name from get_progression; an unambiguous substring is accepted

tools.name: get_demand
tools.description: Residential (low/medium/high density), commercial, industrial, office and storage demand of the loaded city. buildingDemand uses the game's internal 0-255 scale; companyDemand counters can exceed 255. Includes the demand factors that explain WHY demand is high or low (e.g. Taxes, Unemployment, EmptyZones, Homelessness). Positive factor values push demand up, negative values push it down.

tools.name: get_simulation
tools.description: Whether the city is paused, and the current speed. 0 is paused. A positive number is the game speed multiplier.

tools.name: set_simulation
tools.description: Advance the city by in-game time, or pause it. action=advance runs 1-8 in-game hours (default 1, about 20-30 real seconds per hour) at high speed, then restores the previous speed or pause. action=pause pauses immediately and returns; if the city is already paused it stays paused, and the player can resume. Advance returns hours/completed/targetReached/note. Read the city yourself afterward: get_demand, list_notifications, get_services, get_budget. Advance when the next decision needs simulated time; otherwise keep writing. Finish a related group of writes, then one advance (1-2 hours) and one round of re-reads.

action.description: advance runs in-game time then restores the previous speed or pause. pause pauses immediately.

hours.description: In-game hours to advance when action is advance (default 1). Ignored for pause.

tools.name: debug_zone_blocks
tools.description: Dump zone prefab metadata and per-block cell state around x,z for troubleshooting zone growth; use only when asked.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: Capture the current game view as a PNG image. Useful for seeing the city layout, checking what the player is looking at, or verifying the result of an action. Returns the image directly.

tools.name: map_image
tools.description: Undistorted top-down PNG city map in OSM Carto style (roads, rail, buildings by function, parks, water). Names stay in map_text. Omit bounds for a citywide planning overview (road layout, expansion direction, district structure); pass x+z+radius or xMin/zMin/xMax/zMax for a zoomed extent (troubleshooting a site). Returns the image directly.

radius.description: Half-size of square range in meters (with x+z)

tools.name: get_budget
tools.description: Detailed city budget: total income/expenses, balance, and a per-source breakdown (residential/commercial/industrial/office taxes, service fees, subsidies, service upkeep, loan interest, electricity/water import-export, map tile upkeep). Values are monthly rates; expenses are positive costs.

tools.name: get_services
tools.description: Electricity (production/consumption/battery/trade), water & sewage (capacity/consumption/trade), and daily garbage production of the loaded city. Garbage production is the daily amount generated; actual GarbagePilingUp warnings live in list_notifications. Compare electricity/water/sewage supply against consumption.

tools.name: get_labor
tools.description: Employment data: employed citizens, unemployment rate, homelessness, total/free jobs broken down by required education level, and the population age structure (children/teens/adults/seniors).

tools.name: get_statistics
tools.description: Time series of a city statistic (sampled 32x per in-game day). Useful types: Population, Money, Income, Expense, HouseholdCount, WorkerCount, Unemployed, TouristCount, CrimeRate, BirthRate, DeathRate, CitizensMovedIn, CitizensMovedAway, ResidentialTaxableIncome, TrafficFlow-style passenger counts (PassengerCountBus/Subway/Train...). Pass one of those types; any other value returns the full list of valid names.

samples.description: History samples to return. Default 16, max 64.

tools.name: list_taxes
tools.description: Current tax rate and allowed range for each tax area: Residential, Commercial, Industrial, Office.

tools.name: set_budget
tools.description: Single finance write. kind selects the slider: tax (name=Residential|Commercial|Industrial|Office, value=percent, clamped to the allowed range), fee (name=resource from list_fees, value=fee within its slider range), service (name=service from list_service_budgets, value=percent 50-150), loan (value=new loan principal, 0 repays fully, clamped to creditworthiness). Higher taxes/fees raise income but lower demand, usage and happiness.

name.description: Tax area, fee resource or service name (not used for loan)

value.description: New slider value (percent, fee or loan principal)

tools.name: list_policies
tools.description: All city-wide policies with their internal name, localized title, active state, locked state and whether they take a slider adjustment value (e.g. Recycling, Education Subsidies, speed limits).

tools.name: set_policy
tools.description: Activate or deactivate a city-wide policy by its internal name (from list_policies). Slider policies additionally accept an adjustment value; the policy needs to be unlocked.

active.description: true to activate, false to deactivate

tools.name: list_service_budgets
tools.description: Per-service budget sliders (50-150%, 100 = default) with current efficiency, estimated upkeep cost and building count for every city service (police, healthcare, education, transport, ...).

tools.name: list_prefabs
tools.description: Search game prefabs by name and/or typed role. Requires role and/or query. Use role for infrastructure/services; query for name substrings like 'Highway' or 'School'. role=transport includes stations, depots, and roadside stops. role=post includes the post office and mailboxes. category=object lists other roadside objects such as a bicycle rack. Check 'locked' for milestone blocks. Road rows also return road{roadClass, speedKmh, carLanes, highwayRules, zonable}: roadClass is the game's road category (highway = the Highways category), speedKmh is the speed limit, carLanes counts car lanes. Default limit 16, max 64.

category.description: Prefab category (default building); 'net' = all networks incl. train tracks, pipes, power lines, pedestrian paths; 'object' = roadside objects such as stops, mailboxes, and bicycle racks

query.description: Name substring filter. Required if role is omitted.

role.description: Typed capability filter (power, water, sewage, ...). Prefer over name guessing for infrastructure and services. At least one of role or query is required.

tools.name: inspect_operational_area
tools.description: Inspect building-owned operational polygons such as landfill storage or specialized-industry extraction areas. Returns polygon nodes, surface area, current storage/extraction state and capacity/resource requirements. Use index+version from list_buildings.

tools.name: expand_operational_area
tools.description: Expand one owner-linked landfill storage or specialized-industry extractor area to a requested total surface. Keeps the building edge, grows a near-circle around obstacles, and stays on owned land clear of buildings and roads. Extractors rank clear candidates by resource coverage; fertile land, ore, oil and fish use the natural-resource map while forest scans productive trees. Call inspect_operational_area afterward to verify production.

index.description: Building entity index from list_buildings; use an expandable storage or extractor capability

target_area_m2.description: Requested total polygon surface in square metres; must exceed the current surface

tools.name: list_facility_upgrades
tools.description: List installable and already-installed facility upgrades for one building from list_buildings. Returns prefab names plus installed, enabled and locked state. Read-only; use set_facility_upgrade to install a missing upgrade or toggle Out of Service.

tools.name: set_facility_upgrade
tools.description: Install a missing facility upgrade or toggle Out of Service on an installed one. upgrade is a prefab name from list_facility_upgrades. enabled=true installs or returns the upgrade to service; enabled=false sets Out of Service. Do not use place_building for upgrades.

upgrade.description: Exact upgrade prefab name from list_facility_upgrades

enabled.description: true installs or returns to service; false sets Out of Service

tools.name: list_transit_stops
tools.description: List existing transit stops (station sub-stops and roadside stops) with type, position and how many lines already use them. Read-only. Use these entity ids with add_transit_line. A new roadside stop is place_building.

type.description: Optional passenger type filter such as bus, tram, train, subway or ferry

x.description: Optional search center X; with z, keeps the nearest stops inside radius

radius.description: Search radius in meters when x and z are set (default 250)

limit.description: Maximum stops to return. Default 16, max 64.

tools.name: list_transit_lines
tools.description: List transit lines. Optional x/z/radius keeps lines with a stop/waypoint inside the range. Optional type filter. Default limit 16, max 64.

type.description: Optional passenger type filter such as bus, tram, train, subway or ferry

limit.description: Maximum lines to return. Default 16, max 64.

radius.description: Radius in meters (default 250 when center given)

tools.name: add_transit_line
tools.description: Create a simple passenger line. stops is an ordered list of list_transit_stops ids as index:version,index:version. Default type is bus. The line closes back to the first stop and uses native route pathfinding. Vehicles spawn from depots. Do not use place_building for stops or lines.

stops.description: Ordered stop list from list_transit_stops: index:version,index:version. At least two stops of the same passenger type.

type.description: Passenger line type; default bus. Must match the stops.

tools.name: remove_transit_line
tools.description: Delete one transit line from list_transit_lines; stops and stations remain.

tools.name: place_building
tools.description: Place one standalone prefab at x/z. For every site you choose, include radius and omit rotation so the tool can find a nearby legal pose (clearance, road frontage when the prefab needs a road, shoreline snap when it needs water). A roadside object (stop, mailbox, bicycle rack) snaps to the near side of a road or track inside the radius. Omit radius or set rotation for a player-selected exact pose. If exact placement fails, retry with a larger radius and no rotation. Off-road water/sewage/low-voltage nodes receive a matching pipe or cable; high voltage is hand-built. Road-fronted nodes use the networks on that road. Do not use this for regular zoned residential/commercial/industrial/office buildings; those grow from zone.

radius.description: Nearby search radius in meters for sites you choose; omit for a player-selected exact pose. Increase it after a failed exact or narrow placement.

rotation.description: Exact Y-axis rotation in degrees. Omit for sites you choose so prefabs that need a road face the road and shoreline prefabs orient to the wet/dry boundary.

tools.name: build_network
tools.description: Build a road or utility-network connection between two world coordinates. Omit shape for one straight segment. shape=simple is one ramp curve that leaves and joins along the roads at the two ends (departure and arrival, each 0..1 of the end-to-end distance). shape=complex is two segments with a smooth joint; mx and mz move that joint sideways. shape=parallel copies the road between the two given points as a frontage road: each end snaps to the nearest road, offset is required (-80..80 m, positive is to the right walking from start to end) and raise is optional meters up or down (at most 64 road edges per call). Each shape uses only its own fields. Use SHORT segments (50-250m) on OWNED map tiles. An end that hits a compatible node or road edge joins it; a miss starts a new node. The result reports shape, lengthM, steepestGrade, segmentCount and joins. Small streets may join a highway where native validation allows; prefer a ramp/collector/arterial path and verify flowPercent stays at 70 or above via list_networks. For ROAD prefabs, omitting mode selects ground: the route is sampled at roughly 4m or finer intervals for water and local grade, keeping the route on the ground: detected water crossings and grades above 10% (or a stricter prefab limit) call for mode=grade-separated. Use mode=grade-separated for an intentional bridge, elevated road or tunnel; provide both e1 and e2, with at least one nonzero. On a grade-separated road, profile=ease keeps the ends flat (easeStart and easeEnd, each 0..0.5) and profile=arch adds a crest (archHeight, archAt). Pipes, cables and other non-road networks take shape only. Pipes and Ground Cables remain UNDERGROUND by default (auto -10m buried), so omit e1/e2 to accept that burial. If the call fails, change the route or use shorter segments; do not repeat the same coordinates.

prefab.description: Exact prefab name from list_prefabs (category road or net)

shape.description: How the two ends connect. Omit or straight: one straight segment. simple: one curve that follows the road it leaves and the road it joins. complex: two segments meeting at a smooth joint. parallel: a frontage road copied from the road through the two given points. A field for another shape is rejected.

departure.description: simple or complex only. How long the curve follows the road it leaves, as a fraction of the end-to-end distance. Omit to choose from how opposed the two roads are.

arrival.description: simple or complex only. How long the curve follows the road it joins, as a fraction of the end-to-end distance. Omit to choose from how opposed the two roads are.

mx.description: complex only. World X of the smooth joint. Provide together with mz; omit both to place the joint halfway along the ramp curve.

mz.description: complex only. World Z of the smooth joint. Provide together with mx.

offset.description: parallel only, required. Meters to the side of the copied road. Positive is to the right walking from the start to the end.

raise.description: parallel only. Meters up or down from the copied road. Omit for the same height.

profile.description: Grade-separated roads only. Omit or linear: height blends from e1 to e2. ease: the ramp stays flat at each end. arch: a crest above that blend.

easeStart.description: profile=ease only. Fraction of the ramp that stays flat at the start. Default 0.1.

easeEnd.description: profile=ease only. Fraction of the ramp that stays flat at the end. Default 0.1.

archHeight.description: profile=arch only, required. Crest height in meters above the blend from e1 to e2.

archAt.description: profile=arch only. Where the crest sits along the ramp, 0.1 to 0.9. Default 0.5.

mode.description: Road prefabs only. Omit to select ground sampling at roughly 4m or finer intervals, keeping the route clear of detected water crossings and local grades above 10% (or a stricter prefab limit). Use grade-separated for an intentional bridge/elevated/tunnel segment; provide both e1 and e2, with at least one nonzero.

e1.description: Elevation at start in meters relative to terrain (-30..60). Required together with e2 for a grade-separated road, where at least one endpoint must be nonzero; positive values are elevated and negative values are underground. Omit for a ground road or automatic utility burial.

e2.description: Elevation at end in meters relative to terrain (-30..60). Required together with e1 for a grade-separated road, where at least one endpoint must be nonzero. Omit for a ground road or automatic utility burial.

tools.name: list_buildings
tools.description: Find buildings existing in the city by typed service role, operational-area capability, prefab-name substring, or location. Returns roles, capabilities, world position, current entity id and footprint. Prefer role over guessing internal prefab names; use role=garbage for landfills, role=police for police facilities, and role=specialized-industry with operational_area=extractor for farms/extractors. Entity ids change after save reload. Hard max 128 results.

role.description: Typed role such as power, water, sewage, garbage, or specialized-industry

operational_area.description: Require an owner-linked operational area of this kind

radius.description: Radius in meters for spatial filter (default 250 with x/z)

tools.name: list_zone_types
tools.description: All zone TYPES (residential low/medium/high, commercial, industrial, office...) with internal name, area type and locked state. Small type list (not painted cells); use get_zone_counts for per-type cell counts. Use the exact name with zone.

tools.name: zone
tools.description: Paint zoning inside one rotated rectangle along straight road frontage: choose a center, width, depth and rotation that cover fresh zonable strips clear of occupied neighboring blocks. Width follows the rectangle's local X axis; depth follows local Z; rotation is clockwise in world-view degrees. Generic residential/commercial names automatically resolve to the current map theme. Buildings grow while the simulation runs.

zone.description: Zone name from list_zone_types, a generic residential/commercial name that will resolve to the map theme, or 'None' to dezone

width.description: Full rectangle width in meters along its local X axis

depth.description: Full rectangle depth in meters along its local Z axis

tools.name: set_road_features
tools.description: Set composition features on an existing road segment from list_networks: grass, trees, wideSidewalk, soundBarrier, parking, lighting, medianGrass, medianTrees. The road prefab itself changes with replace_road_type.

side.description: Which side for side upgrades (default both)

tools.name: replace_road_type
tools.description: Replace the road between two world points with another road prefab. Each end snaps to the nearest road, then the call follows that road: one edge, or a chain of at most 64. The two points must lie on one connected road. The game clears buildings that grow on the road and names any building needing attention. The new prefab must exist, be unlocked, and be one the game allows as a replacement. Refresh list_networks after success.

prefab.description: Exact replacement road prefab from list_prefabs(category=road)

tools.name: list_networks
tools.description: Inventory of typed network edges for one required kind (road, water, sewage, low_voltage). Isolation QA lives in inspect_network_topology. Shared fields: entity, prefab, start, end, length; distanceM when x/z given. Road also returns widthM, road{roadClass, speedKmh, carLanes, highwayRules, zonable} and traffic{volumeIndex, congestionIndex, activeBottlenecks, flowPercent}. Keep flowPercent at 70 or above; roadClass is the game's road category (highway = the Highways category). Water and sewage are geometry only. Low-voltage also returns electricity{flow, capacity, bottleneck}. Sort: distance (with x/z); traffic_volume|congestion for road; load for low_voltage. Default limit 16, max 64.

radius.description: Radius in meters for spatial filter (default 250)

sort.description: Optional ranking: distance (needs x/z); traffic_volume or congestion (kind=road only); load (kind=low_voltage, highest electricity flow/capacity first)

tools.name: inspect_network_topology
tools.description: Topology QA for one required kind. kind=road: near_miss, unnoded_crossing, too_close_junctions, isolated_road (optional dead ends with include_dead_ends). kind=water|sewage|low_voltage: only isolated_* components that do not reach a road edge. Each finding carries at{x,z}, the repair-site coordinates for build_network. Findings capped at 64. Optional x/z/radius.

radius.description: Radius in meters for spatial filter (default 500)

include_dead_ends.description: If true, also list degree-1 dead ends as facts

tools.name: demolish
tools.description: Demolish (bulldoze) one building from list_buildings or one typed-network edge from list_networks (road, water pipe, sewage pipe, or low-voltage cable), identified by entity index and version. Trees, plants, districts, tracks and other nets are unsupported. Irreversible; double-check the target first.

index.description: Entity index from list_buildings or list_networks

version.description: Entity version from list_buildings or list_networks

tools.name: get_camera
tools.description: Current gameplay camera: pivot (look-at point), position, compass/tilt angles and zoom distance.

tools.name: set_camera
tools.description: Point the gameplay camera: set the pivot (look-at world coordinates; height auto-sampled from terrain unless y given), compass rotation angleX (degrees), tilt angleY (0-89) and zoom distance. Combine with screenshot to LOOK at any place in the city.

y.description: Pivot height (optional, terrain height used if omitted)

tools.name: map_text
tools.description: Compact map text for a range. Returns a local coordinate frame, elevation/slope/water/owned/buildable summaries, connected regions, road nodes/edges, directional sectors, and omitted metadata. Road lines carry roadClass/lanes/speedKmh/highwayRules/zonable; roadClass is the game's road category (highway = the Highways category). Use before choosing an expansion direction or placing shoreline/terrain-sensitive infrastructure. Coordinates in region and network geometry are quantized units relative to frame.origin_world; multiply by quantum_m to recover meter offsets. Spatial evidence for planning. Give x+z+radius or xMin+zMin+xMax+zMax bounds.

radius.description: Half-size of square range in meters (with x+z)

tools.name: probe_layer
tools.description: Compact cell-map probe (landValue, pollution, groundWater, …) for a map range: value min/max/mean plus fixed 8x8 samples. Requires x+z+radius or xMin+zMin+xMax+zMax. If the range covers more than 128 cells, returns truncated=true with a warning and still only 8x8 samples.

radius.description: Half-size of square range in meters (with x+z)

tools.name: get_zone_counts
tools.description: Aggregated summary of painted zones (counts only): cells per zone type with occupied/empty split, whole-city or within an optional x/z/radius. Empty zoned cells are where buildings will grow. Whole-city counts are cheap and safe to call.

tools.name: list_notifications
tools.description: Citywide warning-icon summary. countsByType and topIssues are always complete citywide. Optional x/z/radius and limit filter detail items only (default limit 16, max 64). Use type as a substring filter. Inspect targets with inspect.

type.description: Notification type name substring filter (case-insensitive, optional)

x.description: Optional center X for detail filtering (requires z)

z.description: Optional center Z for detail filtering (requires x)

radius.description: Detail filter radius in meters (default 250 when center given)

tools.name: inspect_entity
tools.description: Detail view of one entity (building/road) by index+version: prefab, position, status flags (abandoned/condemned/destroyed), renters with citizen/employee counts, and for buildings the lot footprint (lotSize in 8m cells / footprintMeters). Like clicking a building in game.

tools.name: get_loan
tools.description: Current loan principal, daily interest rate, daily payment and the city's creditworthiness (max borrowable).

tools.name: list_fees
tools.description: Current price the city charges per service (electricity, water, healthcare, education levels, garbage, parking, public transport...) with slider ranges and estimated monthly income per fee.

tools.name: save_game
tools.description: Trigger a manual save at the player's request. The default name is timestamped.

tools.name: list_tiles
tools.description: List map tiles. filter=owned (default), all, unowned, or available; pass filter=all to list every tile. Every matching tile is returned. Tiles are 623m squares on a 23x23 grid.

tools.name: buy_tiles
tools.description: Purchase one unowned map tile so you can build/zone on it. Give the tile entity index from list_tiles, or gridX plus gridZ coordinates (at least one of the two is required). The game validates permits and funds, charges the tile price and unlocks it. Buy tiles ADJACENT to your current city before expanding roads.

index.description: Map tile entity index from list_tiles

gridX.description: Tile grid X (0-22) as reported by list_tiles

gridZ.description: Tile grid Z (0-22) as reported by list_tiles

tools.name: panel
tools.description: Operate on-screen panels: snapshot returns the pressable controls as a numbered text list; click presses one by its number; fill writes a text box or slider by its number; press sends one key such as Escape. Snapshot again when the screen changes. Covers city settings, the mod list, and saves, including deleting a save. It does not build in the city, and it will not press Send or Stop in this chat.

ref.description: A number from the latest snapshot, such as e1. Required for click and fill.

text.description: Text or slider value for fill.

key.description: One key for press, such as Escape.
